notes.text: The title's own 30 s watchdog: title threads waiting (mostly on pipeline builds) for 30 one-second ticks. #1288 holds it off while a bind waits for a pipeline, so some runs now stall without frames instead of crashing (the "no frames" row).
Three open PRs each add a cap on pipeline waits per frame: #1652, #1931, #2114.
NVIDIA: the removal is made by the user-mode driver at a submission (VidSchErrorDriverFaulted), with no GPU fault, even with every draw and dispatch skipped. Cause not found; no PR.
notes.owner: throny, looking at what is in flight at the stop

notes.text: AMD: XCL_SPLIT_MIDLIST_WAIT=0 took one RX 9060 XT past the world-start hang into the opening cutscene (one run); on NVIDIA it does not. Later traces on the same card show no wait cycle at the hang: an immediate GPU fault 0.9 s after a compute fan-out, with TdrDelay 30 too.
An NVIDIA Aftermath dump points at a race in #455's texture uploads; a one-line wait fixed it in 4 of 4 runs on an RTX 3080. The code it fixes exists only in #455, not in main.
notes.owner: treybertram06, a PR against #455's branch if its author does not take the four lines

notes.text: Past the world load the title's own memory levels off (~6.1 GB on one Linux / RDNA3 box) while the host side keeps growing: XCL's own heap stays at ~0.8 GB, the growth is the shader compiles (RADV / vkd3d-proton) — > 21 GB a minute after the first #101 with disk swap allowed.
The same shape on Windows / RTX 5080: the working set goes 14.8 -> 17.5 GB in the world while the title's commit stays flat; free RAM falls ~30 MB/s and ends runs even on 32 GB.
notes.owner: nobody yet for the driver-side growth; #2527 (XCL_REFUSE_CS) leaves out programs whose compile never ends

notes.text: #1405: 8 of 8 runs faulted without it, 0 of 9 with it (RTX 3090); 3 of 6 against 0 of 3 on a Mac.
Linux / NVIDIA: the vkCreateComputePipelines exception was gone with vkd3d-proton 3.2.0 on one RTX 5090.

On main with the compute split, the stop right after the first #101 (DriverHintX, harmless) is a title thread building the whole form of a split program in bind::execute_indirect -> Chain::whole; XCL_PSO_WAIT_MS does not cover it (RTX 4080, confirmed on an RTX 5070 Ti).
notes.owner: Kalmarv: #2404 runs such an ExecuteIndirect as chained pieces, #2097 splits multi-wave wave64 programs, #2372 builds the whole form in the background

notes.text: #2404 + #2097 on main 68a284a: past the loading screen into the intro cutscene at 0-0.7 FPS (grey frame, no scene geometry), then a device removal at 153.7 s; #2404 alone stayed black until ~508 s behind serial worker builds of two unsplit programs. One run, one RTX 5070 Ti.

With a warm cache (RTX 5080) the ~100 s stop came with five producer-less Wait64 bridged to GPU waits and no watchdog release; XCL_PSO_WAIT_MS=50 presented to 200 s and reached the world, then the title crashed at game+0x4e8b4be.

With the GPU view of the 24 GB pair made readable by copies (an experiment, not a PR) and #541, #2092, #1803, one RTX 3090 got world geometry into the depth target and the G-buffer. #697 is not in the roadmap's list.
notes.owner: adiologydev, a plan for real aliasing of physical pages, before any code

further.text: Once the world runs, the frame rate is set by the CPU: title threads wait on the process heap's lock while XCL creates resources. mimalloc as XCL's allocator took presents from 0.33-0.41 to 1.41-1.64 per second on one Linux / NVIDIA box (2 of its 3 runs then ran out of driver memory). A branch, not a PR.
further.owner: ozimchuk, who would open a PR if the direction is welcome
